surfaces.part: top rail beam and balusters (back railing)

answer.evidence: This is a stairwell seen from above. The back railing (rows 10-19) is a vertical face. Below it, the dark shaft opening (rows 20-29) shows depth inside an open container. The stair treads (rows 30-41) are horizontal bands separated by dark edge lines at rows 34 and 38, so the horizontal surface is visible and foreshortened. The silhouette is 32 px wide through rows 19-38 and narrows to 28 at the bottom. The vertical frame and railing above it give a front face of more than 3 rows, so the object is not a flat slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 7 visible tones per tile, against 3 for floor-flooring and 6 for floor-tatami. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Only 1% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark outlines lean brown and follow the wood. The stair treads and the railing step through about 6 brown values, which matches the tatami reference and is above the flooring reference. The texture is mostly plank and tread banding with few grain dots, so I rate it 'some' rather than 'rich'. It reads as a darker, shaded stairwell and is not a flat sticker. A careful artist would accept it next to these references.
